construction_notes: Employment (Antal ansatte (i arsvaerk)) is measured in full-time equivalent units subject to a minimum activity threshold; workers are counted if they worked at least 80 hours in the given year, were not registered as fully unemployed in the last week of November, and are residents of Denmark.
Employment information is collected via the tax system from compulsory ATP contributions (workers subject to residency registration and minimum annual earnings of roughly 1,300 euros).
A second employment measure, headcount from BFL, is used when FIRM/FIRE employment is missing.
Sales (Omsaetning) and value added (Vaerditilvaekst) come from the accounting statistics, created by DST by combining its own survey with data from SKAT and the Danish Business Authority.
Nominal sales are made real by dividing by the aggregate price deflator, in 2021 prices (DST series PRIS1121).

Section 2.1 states that both sales and value added are measured in thousands of Danish kroner, while the note to Table 1 states that turnover is measured in millions of krone deflated to 2021 values; the figure notes for Figure 3 say thousands of (2021) Danish kroner.
All size variables enter the regressions in log levels.
Firm fixed effects plotted in Figure 4 are winsorized at 0.5 and 99.5 percent.
For the exit analysis the definition of exit is extended to firms exiting in the current year or in the next two years, because firms in their final year are less likely to report.
Size terciles for the exit regression are constructed within sector-age groups, from each firm x year observation's position in the distribution of the variable of interest.
Table 1 reports unconditional descriptive statistics in levels: employment mean 15.7, median 4.0, SD 129.0; sales mean 39.8, median 5.7, SD 613.9; value added mean 12.2, median 2.5, SD 153.7.

key_assumptions.supported_by: Section 3.5 discussion introducing equation (5)

threats_discussed: the firm fixed effects conflate unobservable quality with observable sector and cohort differences
robustness_checks: four versions of the right-hand side of regression (5) are compared in Figure 8
unresolved_confounders: the residual variation is attributed to unobservable firm quality, which is not directly measured

estimator.value: OLS (adjusted R-squared reported)

estimation.specification: Regression (5) with different cohort effects for every sector (sectoral and cohort effects entering multiplicatively) on the right-hand side; the outcome is the firm fixed effect from equation (2), estimated separately for employment, sales and value added.

heterogeneity.dimension: size measure used to estimate the firm fixed effect
heterogeneity.finding: The explained share differs across the employment, sales and value added fixed effects; the paper reports only the range across them, noting that sectoral controls explain more for sales than for employment or value added.

ambiguities: The paper reports a range of adjusted R-squared across the three outcome variables, not a point value, so point_estimate is null and the range is kept verbatim in interpretation.
Figure 8 plots the four bars per outcome variable but prints no numbers.

evidence.annotation: Notes: This figure shows the increase in adjusted R2 from four different versions of regression (5), where we vary the regressions on the right-hand side. We use cohort controls only, sector controls only, cohorts and sector controls entering additively, and cohort and sector controls entering multiplicatively.

evidence.how: Looked in Section 3.5 and in the notes to Figure 8: only a range of adjusted R-squared across the three outcome variables is given in the text; no single adjusted R-squared value, standard error or test statistic is printed, and the per-outcome values can only be read off the bars of Figure 8.
No mean or standard deviation of the estimated firm fixed effects (the dependent variable of regression 5) is printed.
The number of firms entering regression (5) is not printed.

value.as_printed: mu_hat_i = const + sum_{s=0}^{N_s} sigma_s 1_(S_it = s) + sum_{c=0}^{N_c} gamma_c 1_(C_i = c) + sum_{c=0}^{N_c} sum_{s=0}^{N_s} rho_{s,c} 1_(S_it = s, C_i = c) + eps_i.

terms.expression: sum_{c=0}^{N_c} sum_{s=0}^{N_s} rho_{s,c} 1_(S_it = s, C_i = c)

value.parameter_of_interest: the adjusted R-squared of the specification, not a single coefficient
value.normalisation: Equation (5) summarises four specifications; only the stated subset of right-hand-side terms is included in each. The omitted sector/cohort category is not stated.

prior_findings_compared.as_stated: This is in line with the findings in Ma et al. (2025), who document a difference between services and manufacturing in terms of cohorts, which has given rise to superstar firms.

anchor_quote.text: The final multiplicative specification is able to explain between 20 and 30 percent of the variation.
